      intro n hn

      intro k hk

# The orthogonal projection

Given a nonempty subspace `K` of an inner product space `E` such that `K`
admits an orthogonal projection, this file constructs
`K.orthogonalProjectionOnto : E →L[𝕜] K`, the orthogonal projection of `E` onto `K`. This map
satisfies: for any point `u` in `E`, the point `v = K.orthogonalProjectionOnto u` in `K`
minimizes the distance `‖u - v‖` to `u`.

This file also defines `K.starProjection : E →L[𝕜] E` which is the
orthogonal projection of `E` onto `K` but as a map from `E` to `E` instead of `E` to `K`.

Basic API for `orthogonalProjectionOnto` and `starProjection` is developed.

## References

The orthogonal projection construction is adapted from
* [Clément & Martin, *The Lax-Milgram Theorem. A detailed proof to be formalized in Coq*]
* [Clément & Martin, *A Coq formal proof of the Lax–Milgram theorem*]

The Coq code is available at the following address: <http://www.lri.fr/~sboldo/elfic/index.html>
-/

@[expose] public section

variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]
variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
variable [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

local notation "⟪" x ", " y "⟫" => inner 𝕜 x y
local notation "absR" => @abs ℝ _ _

namespace Submodule

/-- A subspace `K : Submodule 𝕜 E` has an orthogonal projection if every vector `v : E` admits an
orthogonal projection to `K`. -/
class HasOrthogonalProjection (K : Submodule 𝕜 E) : Prop where
  exists_orthogonal (v : E) : ∃ w ∈ K, v - w ∈ Kᗮ

variable (K : Submodule 𝕜 E)

instance (priority := 100) HasOrthogonalProjection.ofCompleteSpace [CompleteSpace K] :
    K.HasOrthogonalProjection where
  exists_orthogonal v := by
    rcases K.exists_norm_eq_iInf_of_complete_subspace (completeSpace_coe_iff_isComplete.mp ‹_›) v
      with ⟨w, hwK, hw⟩
    refine ⟨w, hwK, (K.mem_orthogonal' _).2 ?_⟩
    rwa [← K.norm_eq_iInf_iff_inner_eq_zero hwK]

instance [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : Kᗮ.HasOrthogonalProjection where
  exists_orthogonal v := by
    rcases HasOrthogonalProjection.exists_orthogonal (K := K) v with ⟨w, hwK, hw⟩
    refine ⟨_, hw, ?_⟩
    rw [sub_sub_cancel]
    exact K.le_orthogonal_orthogonal hwK

instance HasOrthogonalProjection.map_linearIsometryEquiv [K.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    {E' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E'] (f : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E') :
    (K.map (f.toLinearEquiv : E →ₗ[𝕜] E')).HasOrthogonalProjection where
  exists_orthogonal v := by
    rcases HasOrthogonalProjection.exists_orthogonal (K := K) (f.symm v) with ⟨w, hwK, hw⟩
    refine ⟨f w, Submodule.mem_map_of_mem hwK, Set.forall_mem_image.2 fun u hu ↦ ?_⟩
    simp [← f.symm.inner_map_map, hw u hu]

instance HasOrthogonalProjection.map_linearIsometryEquiv' [K.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    {E' : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E'] (f : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E') :
    (K.map (f.toLinearIsometry : E →ₗ[𝕜] E')).HasOrthogonalProjection :=
  HasOrthogonalProjection.map_linearIsometryEquiv K f

instance : (⊤ : Submodule 𝕜 E).HasOrthogonalProjection := ⟨fun v ↦ ⟨v, trivial, by simp⟩⟩

instance (K : ClosedSubmodule 𝕜 E) [CompleteSpace E] : K.HasOrthogonalProjection := by
  letI := K.isClosed'
  infer_instance

/-- If `K` admits an orthogonal projection, `K` and `Kᗮ` are complements of each other. -/
theorem isCompl_orthogonal [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : IsCompl K Kᗮ where
  disjoint := K.orthogonal_disjoint
  codisjoint := K.codisjoint_iff_exists_add_eq.mpr fun z ↦
    have ⟨w, hw, hzw⟩ := Submodule.HasOrthogonalProjection.exists_orthogonal (K := K) z
    ⟨w, z - w, hw, hzw, add_sub_cancel w z⟩

    ‖K.projection Kᗮ K.isCompl_orthogonal x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ := by
  conv_rhs => rw [← projection_add_projection_eq_self K.isCompl_orthogonal x]
  simp [← sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _), sq, mul_nonneg,
    norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_of_inner_eq_zero _ _ (K.mem_orthogonal _ |>.mp _ _ _)]

  isCompl := K.isCompl_orthogonal
  continuous_projection := AddMonoidHomClass.continuous_of_bound _ 1 fun x ↦ by
    grw [norm_projection_orthogonal_le, one_mul]

/-- If `K₁` admits an orthogonal projection and is contained in `K₂`,
then `K₁` and `K₁ᗮ ⊓ K₂` span `K₂`. -/
theorem sup_orthogonal_inf_of_hasOrthogonalProjection {K₁ K₂ : Submodule 𝕜 E} (h : K₁ ≤ K₂)
    [K₁.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K₁ ⊔ K₁ᗮ ⊓ K₂ = K₂ := by
  ext x
  rw [Submodule.mem_sup]
  let v : K₁ := orthogonalProjectionOnto K₁ x
  have hvm : x - v ∈ K₁ᗮ := sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal x

  · exact fun hx => ⟨v, v.prop, x - v, ⟨hvm, K₂.sub_mem hx (h v.prop)⟩, add_sub_cancel _ _⟩

/-- The inverse of the strict alternating correction operator. -/
def soninProjectionResolvent
    (A B : Submodule Complex H) [A.HasOrthogonalProjection] [B.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    (hT : ‖soninAlternatingBlock A B‖ < 1) : H →L[Complex] H :=
  ↑((Units.oneSub (soninAlternatingBlock A B) hT)⁻¹)

/-- Exact two-projection resolvent formula for the projection onto the common kernel. -/
theorem soninIntersectionProjection_eq_resolventFormula
    (A B : Submodule Complex H) [A.HasOrthogonalProjection] [B.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    [(A.orthogonal ⊓ B.orthogonal).HasOrthogonalProjection]
    (hT : ‖soninAlternatingBlock A B‖ < 1) :
    soninIntersectionProjection A B =
      A.orthogonal.starProjection -
        A.orthogonal.starProjection * soninProjectionResolvent A B hT *
          B.starProjection * A.orthogonal.starProjection := by
  let T : H →L[Complex] H := soninAlternatingBlock A B
  let e : (H →L[Complex] H)ˣ := Units.oneSub T (by simpa [T] using hT)
  let V : H →L[Complex] H := (↑(e⁻¹) : H →L[Complex] H)
  apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext
  intro x
  let xE : H := A.orthogonal.starProjection x
  let u : H := V (B.starProjection xE)
  let c : H := A.orthogonal.starProjection u
  let z : H := xE - c
  have hres : (1 - T) u = B.starProjection xE := by
    change ((↑e : H →L[Complex] H) * (↑(e⁻¹) : H →L[Complex] H))
        (B.starProjection xE) = B.starProjection xE
    rw [← Units.val_mul]
    simp
  have hres' : u - T u = B.starProjection xE := by
    simpa using hres
  have hTu : T u ∈ B := by
    change B.starProjection (A.starProjection (B.starProjection u)) ∈ B
    exact B.starProjection_apply_mem _
  have huB : u ∈ B := by
    have hu : u = B.starProjection xE + T u := sub_eq_iff_eq_add.mp hres'
    rw [hu]
    exact B.add_mem (B.starProjection_apply_mem _) hTu
  have hBu : B.starProjection u = u := B.starProjection_eq_self_iff.mpr huB
  have hTu_eq : T u = B.starProjection (A.starProjection u) := by
    change B.starProjection (A.starProjection (B.starProjection u)) = _
    rw [hBu]
  have hc : c = u - A.starProjection u := by
    simp [c]
  have hcB : B.starProjection c = B.starProjection xE := by
    calc
      B.starProjection c = B.starProjection (u - A.starProjection u) := by rw [hc]
      _ = B.starProjection u - B.starProjection (A.starProjection u) := map_sub _ _ _
      _ = u - T u := by rw [hBu, hTu_eq]
      _ = B.starProjection xE := hres'
  have hxEA : xE ∈ A.orthogonal := A.orthogonal.starProjection_apply_mem x
  have hzmem : z ∈ A.orthogonal ⊓ B.orthogonal := by
    constructor
    · exact A.orthogonal.sub_mem hxEA (A.orthogonal.starProjection_apply_mem u)
    · exact B.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff.mp (by simp [z, hcB])
  have hcSup : c ∈ A ⊔ B := by
    rw [hc]
    exact (A ⊔ B).sub_mem ((le_sup_right : B ≤ A ⊔ B) huB)
      ((le_sup_left : A ≤ A ⊔ B) (A.starProjection_apply_mem u))
  have hxsub : x - xE = A.starProjection x := by
    simp [xE]
  have hxzSup : x - z ∈ A ⊔ B := by
    have hdecomp : x - z = (x - xE) + c := by
      dsimp [z]
      abel
    rw [hdecomp, hxsub]
    exact (A ⊔ B).add_mem
      ((le_sup_left : A ≤ A ⊔ B) (A.starProjection_apply_mem x)) hcSup
  have hsupOrth : A ⊔ B ≤ (A.orthogonal ⊓ B.orthogonal).orthogonal := by
    rw [Submodule.inf_orthogonal]
    exact (A ⊔ B).le_orthogonal_orthogonal
  have hproj : soninIntersectionProjection A B x = z := by
    change (A.orthogonal ⊓ B.orthogonal).starProjection x = z

      (hsupOrth hxzSup)

  change z = xE - A.orthogonal.starProjection (V (B.starProjection xE))

relative-freeness statements.  The exact finite-part/unit reflection makes the latter a nonzero
diagonal transform of the regular-unit coefficient frame, so the existing scale--unit theorem
closes to joint scale--remainder freeness over the moving-center field.
-/

/-- Nonzero rational-base rescaling from regular-unit coefficients to finite-part jets. -/
def gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale : Option ℕ → GammaPoleRationalBase
  | none => 1
  | some m => RatFunc.C (-(m.factorial : ℂ))

theorem gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale_ne_zero (o : Option ℕ) :
    gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale o ≠ 0 := by
  rcases o with (_ | m)
  · exact one_ne_zero
  · have hfac : ((m.factorial : ℂ)) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_ne_zero m
    simpa [gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale] using
      RatFunc.C_injective.ne (neg_ne_zero.mpr hfac)

  | some m => gammaPoleFinitePartJetGerm m

/-- Rational moving-center evaluation on the scale--finite-part frame. -/
def gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval :
    MvPolynomial (Option ℕ) GammaPoleRationalBase →+* NatGerm :=
  MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ratNatEval gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetFamily

    gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval =
      gammaPoleScaleAndUnitPositiveCoefficientRationalEval.comp

          gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale).toRingHom := by

  · intro c
    simp [gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval,
      gammaPoleScaleAndUnitPositiveCoefficientRationalEval,
      mvPolynomialDiagonalScaleRing]
  · intro o
    rcases o with (_ | m)
    · simp [gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval,

        gammaPoleScaleAndUnitPositiveCoefficientRationalEval,

        gammaPoleScaleAndUnitPositiveCoefficientRationalEval,
        gammaPoleScaleAndUnitPositiveCoefficientFamily,
        gammaPoleFinitePartRationalScale,
        mvPolynomialDiagonalScaleRing,
        gammaPoleFinitePartJetGerm_eq_unitCoefficient]

    Function.Injective gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval := by
  rw [gammaPoleScaleAndFinitePartJetRationalEval_eq_comp]

# Finite evaluation Hasse principles for zeta and completed Xi jets

The unconditional finite reconstruction packets for the initial Riemann-zeta jet and canonical
completed-Xi jet are promoted to explicit Hasse data.  Their chosen complex evaluation places
jointly detect coefficient equality and vanishing, reconstruct all global coefficients, and expose
one local witness whenever two global jet combinations differ.
-/

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- Chosen finite Hasse evaluation packet for the initial Riemann-zeta jet. -/
noncomputable def riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData (d : ℕ) :=
  finiteEvaluationHasseDataOf
    (GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.riemannZetaInitialJet_finiteEvaluationHilbertReconstruction d)

/-- Chosen finite Hasse evaluation packet for the canonical completed-Xi jet. -/
noncomputable def xiCanonicalJetHasseData (d : ℕ) :=
  finiteEvaluationHasseDataOf
    (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_finiteEvaluationHilbertReconstruction d)

/-- Chosen point evaluations form a Hasse family for initial Riemann-zeta jets. -/
noncomputable def riemannZetaInitialJetHasseFamily (d : ℕ) :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).hasseFamily

/-- Chosen point evaluations form a Hasse family for canonical completed-Xi jets. -/
noncomputable def xiCanonicalJetHasseFamily (d : ℕ) :=
  (xiCanonicalJetHasseData d).hasseFamily

/-- Initial zeta-jet coefficients are recovered exactly from the chosen local values. -/
theorem riemannZetaInitialJetHasse_reconstruct (d : ℕ) (a : Fin d → ℂ) :
    (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).reconstruct
        ((riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket a) = a :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).reconstruct_localPacket a

/-- Equality of initial zeta jets is detected at every chosen evaluation place. -/
theorem riemannZetaInitialJet_congr_hasse_iff (d : ℕ) (a b : Fin d → ℂ) :
    (∀ i, (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket a i =
      (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket b i) ↔ a = b :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket_congr_hasse_iff a b

/-- An initial zeta jet is zero exactly when every chosen local value is zero. -/
theorem riemannZetaInitialJet_eq_zero_hasse_iff (d : ℕ) (a : Fin d → ℂ) :
    (∀ i, (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket a i = 0) ↔ a = 0 :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket_eq_zero_hasse_iff a

/-- Distinct initial zeta jets differ at one chosen evaluation place. -/
theorem riemannZetaInitialJet_ne_iff_exists_localWitness
    (d : ℕ) (a b : Fin d → ℂ) :
    a ≠ b ↔ ∃ i, (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket a i ≠
      (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket b i :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).ne_iff_exists_localPacket_ne a b

theorem riemannZetaInitialJetHasse_existsUnique (d : ℕ) (packet : Fin d → ℂ) :
    ∃! a : Fin d → ℂ, (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket a = packet :=
  (riemannZetaInitialJetHasseData d).localPacket_existsUnique packet

The initial derivative dictionary `0, ..., d - 1` is collision-free.  Relabeling it by successor
apertures gives `1, ..., d`, so the transverse nonzero-aperture condition also disappears.
Choosing packet size `N + 2` discharges the sharp rank-two condition.  The existing
HTGeometry/HilbertMetric connector then supplies the complete complex and real cofinite

/-- Canonical initial completed-Xi derivative dictionary. -/
def xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder (d : ℕ) : Fin d → ℕ :=
  fun j => j

/-- Canonical derivative orders have no collisions. -/
theorem xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_injective (d : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d) := by
  intro i j hij
  exact Fin.ext hij

/-- The associated successor aperture is the positive label `j + 1`. -/
theorem xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_successorAperture_apply
    {d : ℕ} (j : Fin d) :
    xiDerivativeOrderSuccessorAperture
        (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d) j = j + 1 :=
  rfl

/-- Positive integral aperture packet canonically attached to the initial Xi jet dictionary. -/
def xiCanonicalPositiveAperture (d : ℕ) : Fin d → ℕ :=
  xiDerivativeOrderSuccessorAperture (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d)

/-- Canonical positive apertures have no collisions. -/
theorem xiCanonicalPositiveAperture_injective (d : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (xiCanonicalPositiveAperture d) :=
  (xiDerivativeOrderSuccessorAperture_injective_iff
    (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d)).2
      (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_injective d)

/-- Canonical successor apertures exclude the zero boundary. -/
theorem xiCanonicalPositiveAperture_ne_zero
    {d : ℕ} (j : Fin d) :
    xiCanonicalPositiveAperture d j ≠ 0 :=
  xiDerivativeOrderSuccessorAperture_ne_zero
    (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d) j

/-- Canonical successor apertures lie in the strict positive chamber. -/
theorem xiCanonicalPositiveAperture_pos
    {d : ℕ} (j : Fin d) :
    0 < xiCanonicalPositiveAperture d j :=
  Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (xiCanonicalPositiveAperture_ne_zero j)

/-- Canonical arbitrary Xi jets admit exact complex cofinite Hilbert reconstruction with no
collision hypothesis. -/
theorem xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_cofiniteHilbertReconstruction (d : ℕ) :
    CofiniteEvaluationHilbertReconstruction
      (xiDerivativeOrderFamily (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d)) :=
  (xiDerivativeOrderCofiniteHilbertReconstruction_iff_injective
    (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder d)).2
      (xiCanonicalDerivativeOrder_injective d)

  (exists_injective_xiDerivativeOrderEvaluationHilbertReconstruction_iff

/-- **Intrinsic rational-coefficient joint ladder independence.**  In the canonical
denominator-cleared functional semantics, no nonzero relation over `ℂ(a)` couples a finite family
of Hurwitz ladders whose monodromy monomials are pairwise distinct. -/
theorem joint_hurwitz_ladder_rational_independence
    {s : ι → ℂ} (hs1 : ∀ j, 1 < (s j).re)
    (hmono : Function.Injective (monomialValue (fun j => monoScalar (s j))))
    (N : ℕ) (Q : MvPolynomial (ι × Fin (N + 1)) (RatFunc ℂ))
    (hrel : ∀ a : ℂ, 0 < a.im →
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.evalRingHom a)
        (fun jk => hzeta (s jk.1 + ((jk.2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) a)
        (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.clearRatFuncCoefficients Q) = 0) :
    Q = 0 := by
  have hclear := joint_hurwitz_ladder_independence hs1 hmono N
    (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.clearRatFuncCoefficients Q) hrel
  by_contra hQ
  exact GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.clearRatFuncCoefficients_ne_zero Q hQ hclear

/-- Rational linear independence of `1` and the exponents implies rational-coefficient joint
independence of every finite union of their Hurwitz ladders. -/
theorem joint_hurwitz_ladder_rational_independence_of_linearIndependent
    {s : ι → ℂ} (hs1 : ∀ j, 1 < (s j).re)
    (hsQ : LinearIndependent ℚ (exponentFamily s))
    (N : ℕ) (Q : MvPolynomial (ι × Fin (N + 1)) (RatFunc ℂ))
    (hrel : ∀ a : ℂ, 0 < a.im →
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.evalRingHom a)
        (fun jk => hzeta (s jk.1 + ((jk.2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) a)
        (GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.clearRatFuncCoefficients Q) = 0) :
    Q = 0 :=
  joint_hurwitz_ladder_rational_independence hs1
    (monomialValue_monoScalar_injective_of_linearIndependent s hsQ) N Q hrel

/-- A finite family of Hurwitz zeta functions is jointly hypertranscendental in the shift variable
when the monomials in its monodromy scalars are pairwise distinct. -/
theorem joint_hzeta_hypertranscendental_in_shift
    {s : ι → ℂ} (hs1 : ∀ j, 1 < (s j).re)
    (hmono : Function.Injective (monomialValue (fun j => monoScalar (s j))))
    (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial (ι × Fin (N + 1)) (Polynomial ℂ))
    (hrel : ∀ a : ℂ, 0 < a.im →
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.evalRingHom a)
        (fun jk => iteratedDeriv (jk.2 : ℕ) (hzeta (s jk.1)) a) P = 0) :
    P = 0 := by
  let c : (ι × Fin (N + 1)) → ℂ := fun jk =>
    (-1 : ℂ) ^ (jk.2 : ℕ) * (ascPochhammer ℂ (jk.2 : ℕ)).eval (s jk.1)
  have hc : ∀ jk, c jk ≠ 0 := by
    intro jk
    exact mul_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num))
      (ascPochhammer_eval_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (jk.2 : ℕ) (hs1 jk.1))
  let P' := hzetaJetDiagonalScale c P
  have hrel' : ∀ a : ℂ, 0 < a.im →
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.evalRingHom a)
        (fun jk => hzeta (s jk.1 + ((jk.2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) a) P' = 0 := by
    intro a ha
    change MvPolynomial.eval₂ (Polynomial.evalRingHom a)
      (fun jk => hzeta (s jk.1 + ((jk.2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) a)
      (hzetaJetDiagonalScale c P) = 0
    rw [eval₂_hzetaJetDiagonalScale]
    have hjet : (fun jk => c jk * hzeta (s jk.1 + ((jk.2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) a) =
        fun jk => iteratedDeriv (jk.2 : ℕ) (hzeta (s jk.1)) a := by
      funext jk
      exact (hzeta_iteratedDeriv (jk.2 : ℕ) (hs1 jk.1) (a := a) ha).symm
    rw [hjet]
    exact hrel a ha
  have hP' : P' = 0 := joint_hurwitz_ladder_independence hs1 hmono N P' hrel'
  change hzetaJetDiagonalScale c P = 0 at hP'
  have hinv := congrArg (hzetaJetDiagonalScale (fun i => (c i)⁻¹)) hP'
  rw [hzetaJetDiagonalScale_inv_apply c hc P] at hinv
  simpa using hinv

`a ↦ ζ(s_j,a)` is algebraically independent over `ℂ[a]`.  In particular there is no mixed
algebraic differential equation coupling the family. -/

    (hsQ : LinearIndependent ℚ (exponentFamily s))
    (N : ℕ) (P : MvPolynomial (ι × Fin (N + 1)) (Polynomial ℂ))

        (fun jk => iteratedDeriv (jk.2 : ℕ) (hzeta (s jk.1)) a) P = 0) :

  joint_hzeta_hypertranscendental_in_shift hs1
    (monomialValue_monoScalar_injective_of_linearIndependent s hsQ) N P hrel
